newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanian parliament approves Italian-led force.
newsitem.headline: Albanian parliament approves Italian-led force.

text.p: The Albanian parliament voted on Sunday to approve deployment of an Italian-led multinational security force to protect humanitarian relief operations in the lawless Balkan country.

The parliament, dominated by President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party, voted 97 to 1 to pass the law approving the U.N.-approved multinational force. Italy hopes to start sending security forces to Albania over the next two weeks.
Foreign Minister Arjan Starova told the parliament it was essential that the multinational force be approved and deployed quickly to oversee relief operations and help stabilise the country.

Albania has been racked by violence since January when a number of fraudulent savings schemes collapsed and wiped out millions of dollars. The south then staged a popular uprising against Berisha and remains largely out of government control.

Starova also blamed Italy for the sinking of an illegal Albanian refugee boat on Friday, saying about 79 people were still missing after the accident. An Italian navy corvette was trying to block the refugee boat from entering Italian waters.
